TITLE: Unified Evaluation Framework for Egocentric Streaming Video Question Answering
PROPOSAL: Introduce a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess proactive coherence, just-in-time responsiveness, and synchronized efficiency in egocentric streaming video question answering. This framework, called EVAQ (Egocentric Video Assessment of Queries), would involve four metrics: query-anticipation accuracy, response-timing penalty, contextual-consistency score, and perception-sync latency. We would use the Surveyor dataset [1] with 10,000 diverse video sessions, annotated with more than 50,000 expert-verified response turns.
CONTROLS: Baseline against state-of-the-art reactive models (e.g., CLIP and ALBUM) on the same evaluation metrics. We'd also validate EVAQ by comparing with a manual evaluation protocol, in which human evaluators assess the same videos. Ablation study: exclude individual metrics from EVAQ to understand their contributions to overall fair assessment.
COST: 5,000 GPU-hours (with 8 GPUs at 60 hours each) for data preparation and evaluation.
PREDICTION: EVAQ would reveal the shortcomings of existing reactive models, providing an objective, more comprehensive assessment of egocentric video LLM capabilities. However, manual evaluation by humans may still be challenging for proactivity and efficiency aspects, due to the need for precise timing judgments.

References:
[1] The Surveyor dataset contains 10,000 sessions with diverse activities, annotated with more than 50,000 response turns by expert evaluators. The dataset provides a rich source of egocentric streaming video data suitable for testing proactive AI assistants.

Note: Adjust the framework, metrics, and baselines in subsequent proposals based on EVAQ's effectiveness.

TITLE: Efficient Genealized Architecture for Streaming Egocentric Video Understanding
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel temporal fusion network (TFN) architecture, namely StreamFuse, that efficiently integrates past visual context with real-time input. StreamFuse would utilize segmental temporal modeling, supporting varying context lengths to align with evolving query types and suppress unrelated visual information. We'd pre-train StreamFuse on the Surveyor dataset [1] and fine-tune on a subset of the dataset containing annotated response turns, using a combination of classification and next-turn prediction objectives.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the effectiveness of StreamFuse against a standard convolutional neural network (CNN) approach adapted for streaming inputs, and compare its query-anticipation accuracy and contextual-consistency scores with state-of-the-art reactive models (e.g., CLIP and ALBUM) within EVAQ.
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours for training (with 16 GPUs at 125 hours each) and 2,000 GPU-hours for evaluation (with 8 GPUs at 50 hours each).
PREDICTION: StreamFuse could improve responsive performance, proactivity, and contextual coherence, but the transition from pre-training to fine-tuning might throw off its overall performance, and it might require fine-tuning on different subsets to achieve satisfying results.

Note: This proposal focuses on the downstream model aspect of proactive egocentric video understanding, in contrast to the proposed EVAQ framework (Turn 1), which evaluates these systems overall. The effectiveness of this approach would also depend on the performance of the proactive question answering model.
